newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. senators say rift in North Korea leadership.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators say rift in North Korea leadership.

text.p: North Korea's civilian authorities believe there is a "rift" with the military about participation in Korean peace talks, a group of U.S. senators said on Saturday.

The five senators, who spent the last 24 hours in the North Korean capital Pyongyang, told a news conference in Tokyo that the North Korean officials were very open and forthright about the existence of a rift.
The senators said the military was taking a hard line on the issue of whether the Stalinist nation should receive new food and other aid before agreeing to engage in peace talks with South Korea.
They said the civilian leadership appeared to be more flexible on whether the aid must precede any talks.

"I think that we were led to believe that there is a rift. The military is disturbed that the civilian authorities have not been able to obtain the food and fuel they'd been told they'd get," said Senator Ted Stevens, Republican from Alaska and head of the delegation.

International aid agencies say North Korea, devastated by two consecutive years of floods, is only weeks away from starvation. North and South Korea are locked in a Cold War confrontation since a 1953 truce agreement ended their three-year war.
